original_question: What would be the effect of knocking down the gene associated with Alström syndrome?

final_qi.question: What would be the effect of knocking down the gene associated with Alström syndrome?
final_qi.long_answer: Alström syndrome is caused by mutations in the ALMS1 gene, whose protein localises to the basal body of the primary cilium. Experimental knock-down of ALMS1 (e.g., by siRNA) prevents normal ciliogenesis and maintenance of the primary cilium, yielding cells that lack or have severely shortened cilia and thus display the typical ciliopathy defects seen in Alström syndrome.

0.question: Which gene is associated with Alström syndrome?

final_answer.long_answer: Alström syndrome is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the ALMS1 gene, whose protein localises to the centrosome/basal body of the primary cilium. Experimental knock-down of ALMS1 prevents normal assembly and maintenance of the primary cilium, yielding shortened or absent cilia and consequent impairment of cilia-mediated signalling—hallmarks of the disease phenotype.
